subject: How do you test the differences in the effect of predictors on the outcome across groups ?

messages.author: 992cec4c4574f59a
messages.subject: How do you test the differences in the effect of predictors on the outcome across groups ?
parts:
Hello. I would like to kindly ask you for help with my data analyses.

Here is my question.
I developed 2 structural regression models for Group A and Group B with equivalent predictors and outcome variables.
Now, I want to compare if the effects of the predictor variables on the outcome variables are statistically different across two groups. 

For example, let's say I have "motivation" as a predictor and "achievement" as an outcome variable for male and female groups of students.
Motivation significantly predicts achievement of both gender groups but I want to see if the effect of motivation on achievement is higher for one group than the other (I have already checked the measurement invariance).

How could I do that using R? 
Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: How do you test the differences in the effect of predictors on the outcome across groups ?
parts:
You can fit the models to both groups simultaneously, letting the regression parameter(s) be free across groups in one fitting, and constraining the slope(s) to equality across groups in another fitting, then look at the chi-square difference test.  Details on running a multiple-group model and constraining parameters across groups can be found on the lavaan page:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html

Terry
